name: Adaptation
description: Your body adapts at once to whatever environment you are in, so you can breathe, move, sense and survive in hostile or alien surroundings — underwater you would grow gills and fins and ignore the pressure and cold. No roll and no rank: one purchase covers every environment.

name: Alternate Form
description: You can change into another form, built as a separate character. Its power level can be anything up to yours and sets only its Hero Point budget, never its Trait Cap. Every form pays this Power's full cost, and buying it again adds another form — with two extra forms, all three pay for both. Each form has its own Traits and may share Perks and Flaws. You have one pool of Resolve: the lowest figure any of your forms would have alone.

power_cons.name: Independent Forms
power_cons.description: Each form has its own identity, memory and personality, and they need not get along.

notes: Cost scales with the alternate form's power level: 4/8/12/16/20/24 Hero Points for Street Level through Iconic.

name: Animal Control
description: Roll Animal Control against an animal's Willpower to make it do what you want, whether by domination or friendly persuasion. Like any special effect it lasts 1 page per 2 net successes, rounded up.

power_pros.name: Calling
power_pros.description: You can call to animals out to Extreme Range. They race to you, and the duration only starts once they arrive.

power_cons.name: Only X
power_cons.description: You can only control one category of animal, named at purchase. Worth more if the group is narrow or of limited use, such as aquatic animals.

name: Animal Empathy
description: Animals sense that you understand them. One will not attack you without good reason, such as an injury or young to protect, and even then you may be able to talk it down. No roll and no rank. Actually speaking with animals is the Speech Pro.

power_pros.name: Speech
power_pros.description: You can talk with animals. How intelligent they are, and how they respond, is the GM's call.

name: Animal Mimicry
description: Mimic any natural animal you know, living or extinct, and gain all of its Powers at the lower of its rank and yours — even ones that need body parts you lack. You also take its Agility, Might, Perception and Toughness, capped at your rank, wherever they beat your own. Choosing or changing the animal is a free action, once per page, or twice if you give up your next turn. Magical creatures are the GM's call.

power_pros.name: Enhanced
power_pros.description: When mimicking an animal you may substitute your Power rank for that animal's highest-ranked Trait — one Trait per animal, your choice if several tie.

power_pros.name: Selection
power_pros.description: You can mimic several animals at once and take the best Traits among them, but your effective rank drops by 1d per extra animal.

narrative_constraint: Name the Trait — Agility, Might or Toughness — that your creations hold at your full rank.
name: Animation
description: Bring images and objects to life until the scene ends or you dismiss them. Each has Agility, Might and Toughness plus any Powers it plainly should have: you pick one Trait to sit at your full rank and the rest are at half. They are mindless and act only on your mental commands. Each extra thing animated at once lowers your effective rank by 1d, and an object whose Structure is above your rank cannot be animated.

name: Armor
description: A passive defence against physical and energy attacks, whatever type of damage they deal. An attack whose rank is no more than half your Armor rank cannot hurt you at all unless it has the Penetrating Pro; for Minions, compare their unmodified Threat. Baseline is half your Toughness.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank is half your Toughness rank, rounded up.

power_cons.name: Activated
power_cons.description: The armour must be switched on — a free action — and it stops working if you are knocked out.

power_cons.name: Reactive
power_cons.description: Bracers, a shield or similar that you actively interpose, so it counts as an active defence rather than a passive one.

name: Astral Projection
description: Your astral form leaves your body. In that form you have Invisibility, Phasing (Intangible) and Super Senses (Astral Sight), can choose to be seen, and fly as if you had Flight at your Willpower rank. Your body lies dormant while you are out, but you know immediately if it is moved or hurt.

name: Attuned
description: You are attuned to an aspect of nature, a place, or the cosmos, and know when something dramatic or unusual is about to happen within it. Attuned to a place, you also sense powerful beings arriving and leaving. The narrower the scope, the finer the detail. Basic information is automatic; spend 1 Resolve to ask the GM for more. Answers can be incomplete or misleading but are never false.

name: Aura
description: Your body deals one chosen type of energy damage on contact. Anyone who touches you, or hits you unarmed — even when your passive defence stops the blow — takes an attack at your Aura rank that only passive defences resist. You can also make close combat attacks with it; if you have another close combat attack at this rank or higher, use that rank +1d instead. Mundane objects with Structure below your rank (wood is 6d, bullets and metal 9d) cannot damage you.

power_cons.name: Spines
power_cons.description: Quills or spines inflicting physical rather than energy damage, which means the Power gives you no protection against physical attacks.

name: Banish
description: Roll Banish against the target's Willpower or an active defence to send them to another time, place or dimension, chosen at purchase. You may define yours as resisted by Toughness instead of Willpower; active defences apply either way. You cannot send anyone somewhere harmful or inescapable. You can keep using it on somebody already banished until they are defeated, and a banished character still gets their actions wherever they have landed.

name: Blast
description: A ranged attack reaching Distant Range that deals 1 damage per net success, of one damage type named at purchase. The target resists with the better of an active defence and a passive one such as Armor.

power_pros.name: Block
power_pros.description: An active defence against ranged physical and energy attacks, by shooting them down; never against area attacks. Give up your next action and it becomes a blast duel, a contest of 3 exchanges of Blast against Blast: one at once, one on your next turn, one on your opponent's. The winner hits for successes equal to their own Blast rank, resisted by passive defences only.

power_pros.name: Melee
power_pros.description: You can use the Power as an active defence in close combat, which may change how it looks when you do.

power_cons.name: Subdual
power_cons.description: The Power inflicts subdual damage.

power_cons.name: Weapons
power_cons.description: The Power is skill with a group of weapons, however broad or narrow, and you must be armed with one to use it. Armed, you roll your Blast rank to attack instead of Ability plus Weapon Bonus; the weapon otherwise behaves as normal and deals its usual type of damage.

name: Blending
description: Your colouring shifts to match your surroundings: +3d on Covert rolls to avoid being seen. If you keep still you can also go unseen in plain view, rolling half your Covert rank, halved after the +3d is added.

name: Blind
description: Roll Blind against a living target's Toughness or an active defence. A blinded target takes -3d on attack and active defence rolls unless a Power such as Blind Fighting or Radar compensates. Like any special effect it lasts 1 page per 2 net successes, rounded up. A version that hits another sense is possible, with any effect in combat agreed with the GM.

name: Blind Fighting
description: You do not depend on sight in a fight: you take no penalty for darkness or for an opponent you cannot see, whatever the cause. That cancels the -3d from Powers such as Blind, Darkness and Invisibility.

name: Blink
description: You flicker in and out of reality in a fight — phasing, teleporting round opponents, changing size, however you describe it. Roll Blink instead of Might for close combat attacks and instead of Agility for active defence and movement rolls. If you already have one of those Traits, or a Power such as Evasion, Martial Arts or Strike, at this rank or higher, use that rank +1d instead. Not a Travel Power: you move no faster.

name: Boost
description: Raises one Ability, Talent or Power, named at purchase, up to this Power's rank. It costs what that Trait costs for each rank and takes that Trait's rank as its baseline. It must carry Cons saying when and how it works — without them it means nothing.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals the rank of the Ability, Talent or Power nominated by the player when this Power is purchased.

power_cons.name: Rage
power_cons.description: The Power switches on when you lose your temper, but your Intellect and every Talent drop to 1d while the rage lasts. It always subsides by the end of a scene.

notes: Cost is Special: this Power costs as many Hero Points per rank as the Trait it raises, and uses that Trait as its baseline rank. The player nominates the affected Trait, and the rate follows from it.

name: Buff
description: Spend an action and 1 Resolve: you and every ally in the zone get +1d on every challenge roll until the scene ends, for as long as they stay inside the area. Keeping it up afterwards is a free action. It always ends with the scene. Buffs never stack, even from different characters or Sources.

power_pros.name: Greater
power_pros.description: Spend extra Resolve to raise the bonus by +1d per point, up to +3d for 3 Resolve.

name: Clairvoyance
description: See a distant place as though you were standing in it, at any range. A shielded location needs a Willpower roll against the shielding's rank, and another dimension a Superhuman (6) Willpower roll. You can watch a person or object instead if you know them or hold something that links you, but that does not reveal where they are unless what you see gives it away.

name: Cloud Minds
description: No living being within Distant Range can see, hear or otherwise sense you. A target only gets to resist — Willpower against your Cloud Minds — once you come within Close Range of them or do something that makes your presence obvious. Keeping it up costs 1 action every page.

name: Communications
description: Detect, receive, store and send across whatever networks the setting has, worldwide or further if that fits, with no need for towers or satellites. It works without a roll; breaking into a secure network or channel may take a Technology roll.

name: Constructs
description: Create and reshape objects of solid force — walls, cages, ramps, hands, nets. A construct has Structure equal to your rank and grabs, lifts or pushes with Might equal to your rank. Attack by dropping or hurling them, and defend against physical and energy attacks with momentary shields. They last until the scene ends, you dismiss them or they are destroyed. Each extra construct held at once lowers your effective rank by 1d, on top of the usual multiple action penalty.

power_pros.name: Devices
power_pros.description: You can build complex machines and intricate shapes that imitate other Powers, working like a broad Omni-Power.

name: Danger Sense
description: You sense immediate physical danger, even from something no sense could reach, like a bomb under the floor. Roll it instead of Perception to detect danger, and it replaces Perception in your Edge. You also keep your active defence when surprised, rolling the lower of that defence's rank and your Danger Sense. Baseline is your Perception.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

name: Darkness
description: Fill the zone around you with darkness, fog, smoke or similar, defined at purchase along with what can see through it. You can; everyone else caught in it takes -3d on attack and active defence rolls unless a Power such as Blind Fighting or Radar, or a Super Sense that suits the obstruction, compensates. No roll.

name: Dazzle
description: Roll Dazzle against the Willpower or an active defence of every living being in the zone, allies included. Those affected are stunned for one page — no movement and no actions until after your next turn — then blinded (-3d on attack and active defence rolls, as Blind) for the rest of the duration, which is 1 page per 2 net successes, rounded up. A target already under its effects cannot be hit again, so the duration does not stack.

power_cons.name: Deafen
power_cons.description: Once the stun wears off, targets are deafened rather than blinded: disoriented, at -1d on all challenge rolls for what is left of the duration. Whether Blind Fighting or Radar lets a character ignore that is the GM's call.

name: Deflection
description: An active defence against ranged attacks of one kind, physical or energy, chosen at purchase; never against area attacks. When such an attack fails to hurt you, a free action sends it back, rolling the lower of its rank and your Deflection rank. Deflecting is unlimited, but redirecting two or more on one page costs a cumulative -2d on those rolls. Covering both physical and energy doubles the price to 2 Hero Points a rank.

power_pros.name: Physical and Energy
power_pros.description: You deflect both physical and energy attacks rather than choosing one at purchase. The book prices this as doubling the Power, to 2 Hero Points for each rank.

power_cons.name: Only X
power_cons.description: Only one specific kind of object or energy, named at purchase, can be deflected.

name: Density
description: While dense, use your current Density rank in place of Might and Toughness, and you have Armor at that rank. If you already have one of those Traits at that rank or higher, use it at +1d instead. From 3d your weight rank equals your Density rank, and ordinary floors struggle to hold you much past 6d.

name: Detection
description: Sense the presence and exact location of one thing, chosen at purchase: a kind of energy, matter, being or object, an emotion, life itself. Normally no roll; things that are faint, hidden or hard to notice need a challenge roll at your rank. Unlike other ranged Powers it reaches Extreme Range.

power_pros.name: Long Range
power_pros.description: The Power reaches interplanetary distances — as far as the story needs, out to Plot Device Range.

name: Determination
description: Every 5 Hero Points spent here gives you 1 more Resolve at the start of every issue. It has no rank and cannot be absorbed, drained, mimicked or otherwise affected. Only Heroes can use it.
notes: No rank. 5 Hero Points buys 1 extra starting Resolve per issue.

name: Dimensional Travel
description: Spend an action to travel to another dimension. Your first visit to one lands you wherever the GM decides; after that you arrive where you last left it, or spend 1 Resolve to arrive at another place you know there. Free uses in an issue equal your Willpower; further uses cost 1 Resolve each.

power_pros.name: Portal
power_pros.description: You can open portals others can travel through.

name: Dispel
description: Roll Dispel against the rank of an ongoing Power affecting a being or object in range: success ends that Power's duration. It does not stop the Power being used again. Works on Powers of one Source, chosen at purchase. It also serves as an active defence against Powers that inflict special effects.

power_pros.name: Also X
power_pros.description: You can dispel Powers from more than one Source. Each extra Source adds 1 Hero Point per 2 ranks.

name: Drain
description: Roll Drain against the target's highest-ranked Trait of one Source, chosen at purchase. For the duration — 1 page per 2 net successes, rounded up — their Abilities and Talents of that Source drop to 1d and their Powers of that Source stop working. Traits from other Sources are unaffected and cannot be used to resist.

power_pros.name: Also X
power_pros.description: You can affect Traits from more than one Source. Each extra Source adds 1 Hero Point per 2 ranks.

power_cons.name: Only X
power_cons.description: You can only affect one kind of Trait — Abilities, Talents or Powers. Worth more if it is one specific Ability, Talent or Power.

name: Duplication
description: Spend an action to create an exact copy of yourself, without this Power. Limited-use Powers such as Healing or Dimensional Travel draw on one shared tally. The copy has no Resolve, though you can spend yours for it. It vanishes when either of you is defeated and cannot be made again that scene. Buy the Power again for more copies. The GM may limit or forbid it.

name: Elemental Control
description: Create and control one element, chosen at purchase — fire, ice, gravity, magnetism, plants, sound, weather and so on. Through it you imitate other Powers at this rank, so long as the effect makes comic-book sense for the element: in practice Constructs, a narrow Omni-Power, or both. Matter you create is unstable and gone by the end of the scene.

power_pros.name: Matter Creation
power_pros.description: Matter you create is normally unstable and gone by the end of the scene. With this you can make it last like ordinary matter by spending Resolve equal to its weight rank, minimum 1. Your element must be a type of matter.

power_cons.name: Only Control
power_cons.description: You can control your element but not create it, so you depend on whatever is already in range.

name: Emotion Control
description: Roll Emotion Control against the Willpower of anyone in range to fill them with an emotion or mental state — anger, confusion, fear, love, sadness. The GM decides how they react; the feeling runs anywhere from mild to overwhelming, and reactions tend to be powerful and irrational. Like any special effect it lasts 1 page per 2 net successes, rounded up.

power_cons.name: Only X
power_cons.description: You can only produce one emotion or mental state, named at purchase.

power_cons.name: Pheromones
power_cons.description: The Power is chemical. Targets resist with the greater of Toughness or Willpower. Anyone who does not breathe, is on life support, or is immune to toxins is unaffected.

name: Energy Absorption
description: Absorb one type of energy, chosen at purchase, from a nearby source or an attack that hits you, up to the lower of its rank and yours. Energy attacks at or below your rank cannot hurt you; above it, this is a passive defence. Absorbed energy must be used at once: raise Agility, Might or Toughness to the absorbed rank, or take +1d on all rolls, either until the end of the next page; fire it as a Blast at the absorbed rank; or heal 1 damage per 2 full ranks. Absorbing kinetic energy — every physical attack — triples the price and needs GM approval.

power_pros.name: Also X
power_pros.description: Absorb one extra type of energy per purchase. It cannot be used to add kinetic energy after the fact.

notes: Variable per-rank cost: 1 Hero Point per rank normally, 3 if you can absorb kinetic energy (subject to GM approval).

name: Ensnare
description: Roll Ensnare against the target's Might or an active defence; Aura also works as a passive defence against it. A target bound in your ice, vines or webbing can take no physical actions. Like any special effect it lasts 1 page per 2 net successes, rounded up.

power_pros.name: Line
power_pros.description: A tether of some kind, with which you can reel an ensnared target in, provided their weight rank is no more than your Ensnare rank. A target heavier than you can lift may drag you to them instead.

power_cons.name: Immobilize
power_cons.description: You only pin targets in place. They cannot move, but they can still take any other physical action.

name: Evasion
description: Roll Evasion instead of Agility for active defence rolls, movement rolls, and performing or resisting combat stunts. Not a Travel Power: you move no faster. Baseline is your Agility.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Agility rank.

narrative_constraint: Name the specialisation, and the Ability or Talent it sits under.
name: Expertise
description: A specialisation you name, sitting under one of your Abilities or Talents — Agility: Firearms, say, or Technology: Robotics. Roll this rank in place of that Trait whenever the specialisation applies. Baseline is that Trait's rank.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals the rank of the Ability or Talent the specialisation falls under, nominated by the player when this Power is purchased.

notes: Your specialisation falls under one of your Abilities or Talents (Ch.2 p.28), and that Trait's rank is this Power's baseline. Expertise is normally exempt from Resolve — Ch.5 p.83 exempts it 'except for combat skills' — but it counts at its full rank, and so lowers your opening Resolve, whenever the Trait it falls under is Might, Agility, Toughness or Willpower: the four the Attack and Defense table (Ch.4 p.75) uses to attack or defend. Your GM has the final say.

name: Extra Limbs
description: Extra arms, tentacles, a prehensile tail or the like: +2d on attack and defence rolls when grappling. The GM may give the same bonus to other actions more limbs would plainly help, such as climbing or swimming.

name: Flight
description: A Travel Power: you can fly, and your rank is your top speed on the Speed table. Flying needs room to manoeuvre, so halve your effective rank indoors unless the space is exceptionally large.

power_pros.name: Spaceflight
power_pros.description: You can exceed light speed in open space, crossing interstellar distances — assuming you can survive out there.

power_cons.name: Gliding
power_cons.description: You glide rather than fly, losing at least a storey each page unless you find a rising current.

power_cons.name: Levitation
power_cons.description: You can only rise, descend and hover.

power_cons.name: Slides
power_cons.description: You surf on matter or energy you lay down as you go, so you must stay within Distant Range of the ground or other large solid objects.

power_cons.name: Wings
power_cons.description: Wings need room, so you cannot fly in cramped spaces, thin atmosphere or vacuum.

name: Force Field
description: Project a field that everyone inside uses as a passive defence, at your rank, against physical and energy attacks. An attack whose rank is no more than half yours cannot hurt them at all; for Minions, compare unmodified Threat. It does not stop mental attacks, harmless ambient energy or indirect effects such as Darkness. Raising it takes an action and keeping it up is free. Each extra field held at once lowers your effective rank by 1d. Shape it as you like, from a flat plane to a bubble over you and those adjacent; the Zone, Ranged or Area Pro extends it.

pros_allowed_by_own_text.reason: Ch.2 p.29, the Power's own text: 'Apply the Zone Pro to shield large areas.' Zone/Nova is priced by the base Power's Range and the rulebook prices only Ranged (+2/+1) and Touch (+4/+2); Force Field is Self, which it does not price, so the Ranged grades are the ones offered.
Ch.2 p.29, the Power's own text: 'or the Area Pro to shield large areas at a distance.' Area and Burst are priced the same whatever the base Range, so both grades stand.
Ch.2 p.29, the Power's own text: 'the Ranged Pro to shield things at a distance.' Priced +2 from Close Range and +4 from Touch; Force Field is Self, so the +2 grade is the one offered.

power_pros.name: Inviolate
power_pros.description: When you raise a field, spend 1 Resolve and it also repels every Power effect of its rank or lower, not only direct attacks, and works as a passive defence against mental attacks too.

power_pros.name: Permeable
power_pros.description: Attacks can pass freely through the field in one direction, so you and your allies attack normally from inside it. A field cannot be both Permeable and Inviolate.

power_cons.name: Collapsible
power_cons.description: The field collapses when hit by an attack above your rank. It still defends against that attack, but restoring it costs an action.

power_cons.name: Ward
power_cons.description: The field stops mental attacks rather than physical ones. It is the only kind that can hold someone using Phasing (Intangible).

notes: This Power's own entry (Ch.2 p.29) tells you to apply the Zone, Ranged or Area Pro, so all three are offered here despite its Self range — and T-Kay (Ch.8 p.143) is printed with Force Field 12d (Zone).

name: Form — Energy
description: Turn into one type of energy, chosen at purchase, with Aura and Flight at this rank. You weigh nothing, and neither physical nor energy attacks and effects can touch you. You cannot carry or touch anything, but you are not intangible — objects and force fields can hold you — and whatever affects that kind of energy can affect you.

power_pros.name: Also X
power_pros.description: One extra type of energy you can become, per purchase.

name: Form — Gaseous
description: Turn into a gas with Flight 1d. You are weightless, immune to physical and energy attacks and effects, and can pass through any opening a gas could. You cannot carry, touch or affect anything physical, and whatever affects gases can affect you.

name: Form — Liquid
description: Turn into a liquid or a mass of fine particles such as sand. You are immune to physical attacks but not energy attacks, and fit through any opening a liquid could, yet can firm up enough to handle objects and make physical attacks. Your body is still a physical thing: it can be contained, moved and shoved, including by force fields.

name: Form — Solid
description: Turn into solid matter such as ice, metal, stone or wood. In that form use this rank in place of Might and Toughness, and you have Armor at this rank. If you already have one of those Traits at this rank or higher, use it at +1d instead.

name: Gestalt
description: Needs the Alter Ego Flaw. Your powered form is two people merged: each alter ego is a separate character with their own Abilities, Talents and perhaps Powers. Each alter ego beyond two costs another 3 Hero Points.

name: Growth
description: Grow as large as the Growth table allows for your rank. Use your current Growth rank in place of Might and Toughness, with Armor at that rank and Running at half it. If you already have one of those Traits at the rank this would give, or higher, use your own at +1d instead. From 4d your weight rank equals your Growth rank.

name: Hard to Kill
description: You can be killed, but only by something extreme — beheading, acid, a volcano. Heroes cannot die in standard play, so this mostly tells you how to play the character; in a game where Heroes can die the GM should charge more, between 3 and 6 Hero Points.

name: Healing
description: Heal the injuries of anyone you touch. Your rank is the total points of damage you can heal in a day. The GM may also let it cure a disease, on a successful Healing roll or for Resolve.

power_cons.name: Repair
power_cons.description: Your touch mends inanimate things rather than living ones — androids, machines, robots, vehicles and most technology.

name: Hibernation
description: Enter suspended animation for as long as you like. While in it you barely age and need no air, food or water, you stay fully aware of your surroundings, and you can wake whenever you choose.

name: Hyper Breath
description: Pull or push with gale-force breath: roll Hyper Breath against each target's Might or weight rank, whichever is greater, hitting either everyone within Close Range or one target within Distant Range. 1 or 2 net successes pull the target to you or push them out to Distant Range. 3 or more also knock them prone and cost them their next turn. It also disperses gases, or inhales and holds them for as long as you can hold your breath, with no protection from toxic ones.

power_pros.name: Freezing
power_pros.description: Your breath can also freeze, imitating Blast (cold) or Ensnare, but only within Close Range.

name: Illusions
description: Create illusory sights and sounds of any size up to the whole zone. They are really there, so cameras and microphones pick them up. Observers believe them unless they have reason to doubt, and then roll Perception against your rank to see through them. A hand passes straight through and gives the illusion away, unless it is laid over a real object.

power_pros.name: Mental
power_pros.description: The illusions exist only in living minds: cameras and microphones register nothing, and a doubting observer rolls Willpower rather than Perception. A victim can be made to believe they are blinded, bound, hurt or helpless, which works like Stun, rolling your Illusions rank against their Willpower — one target at a time unless you also have the Zone Pro.

name: Immortality
description: You cannot die, or do not stay dead, and you will not die of old age. Heroes cannot die in standard play, so this mostly tells you how to play the character; in a game where Heroes can die the GM should charge more, between 6 and 12 Hero Points.

power_cons.narrative_constraint: Describe how you can be killed.
power_cons.name: Vulnerable
power_cons.description: You can be killed, though not easily. Describe how.

name: Immunity
description: Each immunity is named and paid for separately, at 3 Hero Points apiece: a type of physical attack or weapon; a type of energy other than kinetic; environmental hazards (pressure, radiation, temperature); fatigue and the need for sleep; life support (no need to breathe, eat or drink, plus airborne toxins); negative mental states such as fear; sensory overload such as Dazzle; or toxins (disease, drugs, poison). You may invent others.
notes: Cost is 3 Hero Points per immunity selected.

name: Inanimate
description: You are not alive in the usual sense — a construct, robot, undead, spirit. You are immune to physical attacks and to Powers that only work on living beings, helpful ones included, and in effect you have Immunity (Life Support, Toxins). Your mind or spirit remains, so mental attacks and Powers still work on you. It has no rank and cannot be absorbed, drained, mimicked or otherwise affected. Its Source, which cannot be Trained, says what kind of being you are.

power_pros.name: Mindless
power_pros.description: You have neither mind nor spirit — a true robot, or an animated skeleton — so mental attacks and Powers cannot touch you either.

name: Invisibility
description: Turn invisible. Enemies who cannot see you take -3d on attack rolls and active defence rolls against you unless a Power such as Blind Fighting or Radar compensates. That drops to -2d for enemies who can detect you some other way — other senses, Attuned, Radar, Super Senses, or signs such as footprints and disturbed rain.

power_pros.name: Cloaking
power_pros.description: Turning invisible also hides you from Radar, every vision-based Super Sense, and sensors and equipment that would otherwise pick you up.

power_cons.name: Jamming
power_cons.description: You cannot turn invisible, but you can make yourself undetectable to Radar, vision-based Super Senses and equivalent sensors.

name: Irritant
description: Fill the zone with a sandstorm, gale, noxious gas, insect swarm or similar. Everyone in it but you takes -2d on all challenge rolls except passive defence rolls, unless their Toughness is higher than your rank — no roll is made. You may define yours as resisted by Willpower instead. Starting it takes an action; keeping it up is free.

name: Languages
description: Beyond the one or two languages everybody has, you speak extra languages equal to your Intellect. Name them in advance or as they come up in play.

power_pros.name: Hyper Translation
power_pros.description: You are instantly fluent in any language you meet, barring ones your voice cannot produce or your senses cannot perceive.

power_pros.name: Polyglot
power_pros.description: Languages come naturally. You can get by in a new one within a day or two and master it in about a week.

name: Leadership
description: While you can see and communicate with your team, a free action lets each ally reroll one challenge roll. Each ally gets one such reroll in a combat scene.

name: Leaping
description: A Travel Power: jump the distance the Leaping table gives for your rank, and straight up as though your rank were 1d lower. It needs overhead clearance, so indoors your rank is capped at your Agility for movement rolls. Also an active defence against falling damage. Baseline is half your Might.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank is half your Might rank, rounded up.

name: Life Drain
description: Roll Life Drain against a touched living target's Toughness or an active defence, dealing 1 damage per net success. You may define yours as resisted by Willpower instead of Toughness; active defences apply either way. If you are wounded you heal 1 for every 2 full points dealt. You need not be wounded to use it.

power_pros.name: Vampirism
power_pros.description: The Power deals physical damage, so targets resist it like any physical attack — Armor, half Toughness, or an active defence. It can attack inanimate objects and beings, but you only heal from damage dealt to the living.

name: Light / Effect
description: Generate visible light, or ultraviolet if you prefer, as a free action with no effort. Fill the zone around you, or narrow it to a beam or harmless laser reaching Distant Range. It can be as bright as you like short of incapacitating anyone — that is Dazzle. Bought as Effect, it produces some other harmless but useful environmental effect instead.

name: Lightning Reflexes
description: Your Edge goes up by 6. Any weapon you carry can also be drawn or put away in an instant, which under the Gritty Combat Rules means nobody can get the drop on you.

power_cons.name: Fighting/Marksmanship
power_cons.description: The Power applies only to close combat or only to ranged combat, and you can only quick-draw that type of weapon.

name: Luck
description: At the start of every issue you get Luck dice equal to your rank. Spend them on any challenge roll that involves you: add them to your own roll (3 dice is +3d), or roll them against somebody acting against you and take your successes off theirs. Spending them is automatic and takes no action.

power_pros.name: Control
power_pros.description: You alter probability on purpose. Use Luck on yourself or anyone you choose within Distant Range, as a free action at any time, not only on your turn, so long as you are conscious and aware.

power_pros.name: Unbelievable
power_pros.description: Spend Luck dice on lucky breaks (Chapter 5) as well. Breaks bought this way tend to be more extreme and unlikely than ones bought with Resolve, and still need the GM's approval.

name: Machine Control
description: Control machines and electronics within Distant Range — hack a computer, shut off a camera, drive a car remotely — rolling this rank in place of whatever Trait would normally operate the device. Each extra machine controlled at once lowers your effective rank by 1d, on top of the usual -2d for multiple attacks or actions in combat.

power_cons.name: Interface
power_cons.description: You can only control computers — which still covers any machine a computer controls.

name: Martial Arts
description: Roll it to make and to defend against close combat attacks, in place of Might for grabs, holds, escapes and combat stunts, and in place of your Ability when attacking or defending with a mundane melee weapon (the Gear Limit still applies). Unarmed it deals subdual damage, unlike most attack Powers; a lethal weapon still deals lethal damage. Baseline is your Might.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Might rank.

power_pros.name: Deflect
power_pros.description: Use Martial Arts as an active defence against ranged physical and energy attacks, though not area attacks.

power_pros.name: Deflect Missiles
power_pros.description: Use Martial Arts as an active defence against ranged physical attacks, though not area attacks.

name: Master of Disguise
description: Build a very convincing disguise in one short scene or less, given materials — household goods will do in a pinch — and imitate other people's voices and mannerisms. Roll Charm, usually against the target's Perception. An Item Con on this Power has to mean more than needing supplies, which is assumed.

name: Matter Chameleon
description: Take on the properties of an object you touch for the rest of the scene. It works as Solid Form at the lower of your rank and the object's Structure. You also gain Aura from any energy it gives off, such as lava's heat, at the lower of your rank and that energy's rank. That energy only hurts you if its rank is above yours, and then this Power is a passive defence against it.

name: Mind Blast
description: Roll Mind Blast against a living target's Willpower to deal psychic damage, 1 per net success. It does nothing to inanimate objects and passes straight through them, unless they have a psychic presence.

name: Mind Control
description: Roll Mind Control against the Willpower of a living being within Distant Range; they do as you wish for the duration, 1 page per 2 net successes (rounded up). Or spend 1 Resolve to plant a suggestion that triggers later — even years on — with the duration starting then. Targets get +2d to resist commands that are self-destructive or wholly against their nature.

power_cons.name: Hypnosis
power_cons.description: You need a calm face-to-face conversation with the target first, which makes it useless in combat.

power_cons.name: Pheromones
power_cons.description: The Power is chemical. Targets resist with the greater of Toughness or Willpower. Anyone who does not breathe, is on life support, or is immune to toxins is unaffected.

name: Nullify
description: A dampening field over everyone in the zone, allies included, against Traits of one Source chosen at purchase. Any such Trait ranked at or below your Nullify rank is shut down with no roll: Abilities and Talents drop to 1d and Powers stop. Holding it takes concentration — half speed, and no attacks, active defences or other actions unless you spend 1 Resolve. A target can pay 1 Resolve for each page or use to force a nullified Trait to work.

power_pros.name: Also X
power_pros.description: You can nullify Traits from more than one Source. Each extra Source adds 1 Hero Point per rank.

name: Omni-Power
description: Mimic other Powers at this rank, switching instantly. Every use after the first on a page — any action, movement or challenge roll with it — lowers your effective rank by 1d for the rest of that page, separately from the multiple action penalty. A Power with no rank can only be mimicked if your current rank is at least its Hero Point cost. Add a Pro to a mimicked Power for 1 Resolve, or 2 if the Pro costs 4 Hero Points or more. Narrow versions cover a limited set of abilities and broad ones a wide array; say which, and what it does, at purchase.
notes: Variable per-rank cost: narrow Omni-Powers cost 3 Hero Points per rank, broad ones 5. Cannot mimic Alternate Form, Determination, Inanimate, Life Drain, Luck, Nullify, Power Absorption, Power Mimicry, Preparation, Slay or Time Stop.

name: Phasing
description: Shift out of phase with the physical world. You are immune to physical attacks and effects, energy included, but not to mental ones, and you pass through solid objects but not force fields. While phased you cannot carry, touch or affect anything physical. Switching it on or off is a free action, though never both on one turn.

power_pros.name: Intangible
power_pros.description: Ordinary force fields cannot hold you. Ones with the Ward Con still can, unless your Willpower beats their rank.

name: Plasticity
description: Your body is elastic: reshape yourself and squeeze through the tightest gap. Shapes produce effects at this rank — a ball imitates Leaping, wrapping round something holds it in place of Might, and you can parachute anything whose weight rank is no more than your rank. In combat it is a passive defence against physical attacks, not energy, and replaces Might for grappling and close combat attacks. If your Might is higher than this rank, use Might +1d instead.

name: Polymorph
description: Roll Polymorph against a living target's Toughness or an active defence to turn them into something harmless or helpless — a frog, a sheep, a statue. You may define yours as resisted by Willpower instead of Toughness; active defences apply either way. The change lasts for the duration, 1 page per 2 net successes (rounded up).

name: Portable Storehouse
description: Produce mundane weapons, armour, gear and even vehicles wherever you are — teleported from a warehouse, pulled from a magic bag, made from thin air. They vanish when the scene ends unless you have Resources or Wealth, in which case they may simply be your own things fetched from storage.

name: Possession
description: Roll Possession against the Willpower of a living being within Distant Range to take over their body. You use the host's physical Abilities, Talents and Powers and your own mental ones, the GM deciding which is which. Your own body lies dormant, though you know at once if it is moved or hurt, and you return to it automatically if the host is knocked out or killed. Like any special effect it lasts 1 page per 2 net successes, rounded up.

power_pros.name: Meld
power_pros.description: Your body merges into the one you possess for the duration.

name: Power Absorption
description: By touch, roll against the target's highest-ranked Trait of one Source (chosen at purchase) or an active defence. On a success they fall unconscious and you hold their Abilities, Talents and Powers of that Source, at their ranks, for the duration — 1 page per 2 net successes, rounded up. A Trait you already have at that rank or higher is unchanged. Holding several characters' Traits at once lowers your effective rank by 1d per extra character. It needs physical contact: a target fully sealed in artificial armour or a force field is safe.

power_pros.name: Also X
power_pros.description: You can absorb Traits from more than one Source. Each extra Source adds 1 Hero Point per rank.

power_cons.name: Only X
power_cons.description: You can only absorb one kind of Trait — Abilities, Talents or Powers. Worth more if it is one specific Trait.

name: Precognition
description: Spend Resolve to undo something that has just happened. In combat this erases a character's turn, and you take your own next turn immediately, before they take theirs again. Declare it by the time that character finishes their turn; once somebody else starts acting you can go back no further than the start of that turn. It costs 1 Resolve the first time in a scene, 2 the second, 3 the third and so on. Resolve and Adversity spent in the erased turn stay spent. The GM may disallow it.

name: Power Mimicry
description: By touch, roll against the target's highest-ranked Trait of one Source (chosen at purchase) or an active defence. On a success you copy their Abilities, Talents and Powers of that Source, at their ranks, for the duration — 1 page per 2 net successes, rounded up — and the target loses nothing. A Trait you already have at that rank or higher is unchanged. Copying several characters at once lowers your effective rank by 1d per extra character. It needs physical contact: a target fully sealed in artificial armour or a force field is safe.

power_pros.name: Also X
power_pros.description: You can mimic Traits from more than one Source. Each extra Source adds 1 Hero Point per rank.

power_cons.name: Only X
power_cons.description: You can only mimic one kind of Trait — Abilities, Talents or Powers. Worth more if it is one specific Trait.

name: Preparation
description: Any Hero can spend 1 Resolve to narrate a minor detail into the scene. With this Power that narration goes much further whenever research and planning would explain it: you brought exactly the right mundane item, you prepared this location beforehand, you already have the information, you know or have pull with an Extra. The GM can still veto anything unreasonable. It has no rank and cannot be absorbed, drained, mimicked or otherwise affected.

name: Psi-Screen
description: Roll Psi-Screen instead of Willpower to defend against mental attacks and to resist mental damage and effects. You know when someone uses Telepathy to read your surface thoughts, and you roll this to resist that and any attempt to probe your mind. Baseline is your Willpower.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Willpower rank.

power_pros.name: Cloak Mind
power_pros.description: You can hide your mental presence. A telepath must beat your Psi-Screen rank to detect you at all.

name: Psychometry
description: Touch an inanimate object and ask the GM for its basic history. Spend 1 Resolve to ask in depth about one person or event connected to it, if there is anything to learn. Answers may be incomplete or misleading, but they are never false and must address what you asked.

name: Quick Change
description: Change your clothes and grooming — hair, make-up — in an instant; say how it works. It takes an action.

power_cons.name: Costume
power_cons.description: You can only switch between your costume and whatever you were wearing when you last changed.

name: Radar
description: A radar sense that gives you a three-dimensional picture of your surroundings. It cannot read flat images such as print, photographs or screens. It compensates for the -3d of fighting without sight that Blind, Darkness and Invisibility impose.

power_cons.name: Sonar
power_cons.description: The Power only works underwater.

power_cons.name: Tremor Sense
power_cons.description: You read vibrations in the ground instead, so you only detect things touching the ground or shaking it.

name: Regeneration
description: You heal 1 point of damage every hour. If knocked unconscious you wake as soon as you have healed 1 point, unless somebody revives you first.

power_pros.name: Fast
power_pros.description: You heal 1 point of damage per minute rather than per hour.

power_pros.name: Instant
power_pros.description: You heal 1 point of damage per page rather than per hour.

name: Resistance
description: Roll Resistance instead of Toughness against radiation, extremes of temperature and toxins — disease, drugs, poison. Baseline is your Toughness.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Toughness rank.

name: Running
description: A Travel Power: your rank is your top speed on the Speed table, whether you run, roll, skate or bounce. The 3d baseline is ordinary human running speed, so every rank bought is speed beyond that.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank is a flat 3d regardless of any Ability.

power_pros.name: Hover
power_pros.description: You float a foot off the ground while moving, ignoring caltrops, pressure plates, tripwires, broken ground and the like.

name: Separation
description: Detach parts of your body with none of the usual consequences. Each part acts on its own and can do whatever a healthy detached part plausibly could, your other Powers included: a hand can crawl about and handle objects, and if you can fly, it probably can too.

name: Shockwave
description: Roll Shockwave against the greater of Might or weight rank for everyone in the zone, allies included. 1 or 2 net successes: the target is pushed away — no longer adjacent, still within Close Range — and takes -1d on all challenge rolls until after your next turn. 3 or more: they are also knocked prone and lose their next turn. It shatters fragile materials such as ordinary glass and ice in the area.

name: Shrinking
description: Shrink as small as the Shrinking table allows for your rank, your weight rank falling by your current Shrinking rank to a minimum of 0d. Use that rank in place of Agility, with Leaping and Strike at half it. If you already have one of those Traits at the rank this would give, or higher, use your own at +1d instead. Your size can also make it easier to hit human-sized enemies and to avoid their attacks.

name: Slay
description: Roll Slay against a touched living target's Toughness or an active defence, dealing 2 damage per net success. Armor does nothing against it. You may define yours as resisted by Willpower instead of Toughness; active defences apply either way.

power_pros.name: Lethal Disease
power_pros.description: The damage lands at the end of the issue rather than at once, leaving the target incapacitated until then. Whether a cure is possible before that, and how hard it is, is the GM's call. Symptoms may take days or weeks to show.

notes: Lethal Disease is printed in Ch.7's Toxins section (p.108), not with the Power's own entry in Ch.2. Toxin Pros and Cons apply only to mundane diseases, drugs and poisons unless the GM rules otherwise.

name: Slick
description: Make any of the ground in the zone slippery until the scene ends or you dismiss it. Anyone crossing rolls Agility against your rank or falls prone. Standing takes an action and another Agility roll against your rank; until they make it they cannot leave on foot and take -2d on attack and active defence rolls. A driver rolls Vehicles against your rank or loses control and crashes.

name: Speak with Dead
description: Briefly animate a dead body — or at least its head — and ask it as many questions as your rank. It must answer truthfully, but knows only what it knew in life and speaks only a language it knew.

name: Specialty
description: Free, and only in Street Level and Low Level games. Each Hero picks one Specialty that no other Hero has. It gives +1d on a particular kind of challenge roll, even past the Trait Cap, and on those rolls you can spend 1 Resolve to make your 6s explode: reroll each 6 for more successes, and keep rerolling while 6s come up. The GM may allow one combat and one non-combat Specialty each. It has no rank and cannot be absorbed, drained, mimicked or otherwise affected.
notes: Free, and restricted to Street Level and Low Level games. Each Hero may have only one, and no two Heroes may share one.

name: Spinning
description: Spin at superhuman speed. Roll Spinning in place of Might for close combat attack and defence rolls and for grabs, holds, escapes and combat stunts, and in place of Agility to defend against physical attacks, not energy. If the Ability is at this rank or higher, use it at +1d instead. You can still move, talk and interact normally.

name: Star Gate
description: Spend an action to transport yourself instantly to a distant world. Your first visit to one lands you wherever the GM decides; after that you arrive where you last left it, or spend 1 Resolve to arrive at another place you know there. Free uses in an issue equal your Willpower; further uses cost 1 Resolve each.

power_pros.name: Portal
power_pros.description: You can open portals others — ships included — can travel through.

name: Stretching
description: Stretch or extend your body to make close combat and grappling attacks on targets who are not adjacent. What you pay sets the reach: Close Range for 1 Hero Point, Distant for 3, Extreme for 6. Out of combat, those are about how far you can reach.

power_cons.name: Long Reach
power_cons.description: You have long reach but cannot stretch your whole body.

notes: Variable flat cost by reach: 1 Hero Point for Close Range, 3 for Distant Range, 6 for Extreme Range.

name: Strike
description: A close combat attack — claws, energised fists, a signature weapon — that deals 1 damage per net success, of one damage type named at purchase. Roll it both to attack and to defend in close combat. Baseline is the greater of your Might and your Martial Arts.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank is the greater of your Might and your Martial Arts effective rank. Under the Brute Option, only half your Might counts.

power_pros.name: Deflect
power_pros.description: Use Strike as an active defence against ranged physical and energy attacks, though not area attacks.

power_pros.name: Deflect Missiles
power_pros.description: Use Strike as an active defence against ranged physical attacks, though not area attacks.

power_pros.name: Reach/Throw
power_pros.description: You can hit targets within Close Range who are not adjacent, either through unusual reach or by throwing whatever you strike with.

power_pros.name: Sweep
power_pros.description: An area attack on everyone — friend and foe — in a 90-degree arc reaching 5 to 25 feet from you, or out to 50 feet if the Power also has Reach. You choose how far it reaches each time.

power_cons.name: Subdual
power_cons.description: The Power inflicts subdual damage.

power_cons.name: Weapons
power_cons.description: The Power is skill with a group of weapons, however broad or narrow, and you must be armed with one to use it. Armed, you roll your Strike rank instead of Ability plus Weapon Bonus, both to attack and to defend in close combat; the weapon otherwise behaves as normal and deals its usual type of damage.

notes: Baseline rank is Might or Martial Arts, whichever is greater. Under the Brute Option (Overkill applied to Might) only half your Might counts toward this baseline.

name: Stun
description: Roll Stun against a living target's Toughness or an active defence to take them out of the action — stunned, paralysed, asleep. A stunned target cannot move or act. You may define yours as resisted by Willpower instead of Toughness; active defences apply either way. Like any special effect it lasts 1 page per 2 net successes, rounded up.

power_pros.name: Non-Lethal Disease
power_pros.description: The target is not incapacitated but takes a -2d penalty to every challenge roll for the rest of the issue. Whether a cure is possible before that, and how hard it is, is the GM's call. Symptoms may take days or weeks to show.

power_cons.name: EMP
power_cons.description: The Power affects characters with Inanimate from a Tech Source instead of living beings, and disables most electronics.

power_cons.name: Caustic
power_cons.description: The target is not incapacitated but takes a -2d penalty to every challenge roll while the Power lasts. Delivered as a gas, it attacks everyone in its area at the start of each page.

notes: Caustic and Non-Lethal Disease are printed in Ch.7's Toxins section (p.108), not with the Power's own entry in Ch.2. Toxin Pros and Cons apply only to mundane diseases, drugs and poisons unless the GM rules otherwise.

name: Summoning
description: Call Minions to serve you. Your rank sets how many you can summon in a scene, on the Summoning table. Their Threat is fixed at purchase, up to the Trait Cap -6d, or -3d if you can summon no more than 10 a scene, and the price is 1 Hero Point a rank for every 2d of Threat, rounded up. They fight in close combat unless you add the Shooters Pro. Summoning takes an action, and they act on the page they appear.

power_pros.name: Animals
power_pros.description: Your Minions are animals, with abilities to match such as keen senses and speed beyond a human's; agree the details with your GM. +1 per rank for a narrow selection of animals, +2 for a wide variety with different abilities.

power_pros.name: Automatons
power_pros.description: Your Minions have the Inanimate (Mindless) Power.

power_pros.name: Duplicates
power_pros.description: Your Minions are copies of you. They work as ordinary Minions, rolling Threat for everything, but share your distinctive abilities: if you can fly or phase through walls, so can they. Large numbers of duplicates have big narrative uses, so agree expectations with your GM.

power_pros.name: Shooters
power_pros.description: Your Minions can attack at Distant Range as well as in close combat.

power_pros.name: Unique
power_pros.description: Your Minions have abilities that would be Powers on a full character — acute senses, flight, walking through walls — agreed with the GM and subject to their approval. +1 per rank for a minor advantage, +2 for a moderate one, +4 for a major one.

notes: Cost is Special: 1 Hero Point per rank for every 2d of Threat given to the Minions (rounded up). Threat rank is chosen at purchase, capped at Trait Cap - 6d, or Trait Cap - 3d if you summon no more than 10 Minions per scene.

name: Super Senses — Acute (X)
description: One sense, chosen at purchase, is hyper-acute: roll this rank instead of Perception for challenge rolls using that sense, though not for your Edge. Baseline is your Perception. All Super Senses count as one Power, ranked at the greater of your Perception and this.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Analytic (X)
description: Concentrate with one sense, chosen at purchase, to learn the basic physical properties of something, including its chemical make-up and whether it is organic.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Astral Sight
description: See into the astral realm, the psychic energy tied to the physical world. You can interact with invisible spirits and characters using Astral Projection, and you detect living beings hidden by Powers such as Blending or Invisibility.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Circular Vision
description: You effectively see all around you at once, a full 360 degrees.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Enhanced Hearing
description: Hear sounds too faint, distant or muffled for a human ear with a Perception roll; the GM sets the threshold, at 4 or higher. You also hear infrasound and ultrasound.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Hypersensitive Touch
description: Your touch is fine enough to read print with your fingertips, or to tell what is happening in the next room from the vibrations in a door or wall.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Lie Detection
description: You know when someone within Close Range is lying. No roll, unless they are somehow protected from it, which may call for a Perception roll.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Microscopic Vision
description: Concentrate to see microscopic detail, down to the atomic or quantum scale — whatever magnification the story needs.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Night Vision
description: You can see in absolute darkness, which Ultra Vision and its starlight cannot do.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Radio Hearing
description: You can hear radio frequencies and intercept radio transmissions.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Telescopic Vision
description: Make out small details at extreme distances — as far as the story needs.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Thermal Vision
description: See heat, which lets you see through thin objects, follow the faintest leftover warmth, and see in the dark. Extreme ambient temperatures, or a being whose body exactly matches its surroundings, can defeat it.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Tracking Scent
description: Identify, recognise and track people by scent, and even read their emotional state. Each takes a Perception roll against a threshold of 4 to 6 in ideal conditions.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — True Sight
description: Concentrate to see a being's true form through any disguise, illusion or transformation, Blending and Invisibility included. No roll, unless the subject is somehow shielded, which may call for a Perception roll.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — Ultra Vision
description: See ultraviolet light, and see in light as dim as starlight — but not in absolute darkness.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Senses — X-Ray Vision
description: Concentrate to see through solid objects.

prerequisite.description: Baseline rank equals your Perception rank.

notes: The rulebook treats all Super Senses options as a single Power whose effective rank is the greater of your Perception and your Acute rank. Each option is bought and paid for separately.

name: Super Speed
description: A Travel Power and more. You run at this rank's speed, your Agility effectively equals this rank, and your Edge is this rank times 3. Roll it to make and defend against close combat attacks, and in place of Might to defend in a grapple. At 9d or more you cross 2 range classes a page, run across water and up walls, defeat 2 Minions per net success in close combat, and effectively have Quick Change and Vanish.

name: Swimming
description: A Travel Power: your rank is your top speed through water. You also breathe water, move and sense as freely beneath it as in air, and are immune to the pressure and temperature of the deep ocean.

power_cons.name: Lungs
power_cons.description: You cannot breathe water, though you can hold your breath a long time.

name: Swing Line
description: A Travel Power: swing, climb and descend between anchor points. Outdoors only, or in an indoor space with room overhead, and something stable to tether to — a building, a tall tree — must stay within Distant Range. Your lines have Structure equal to half your rank.

power_cons.name: Natural
power_cons.description: You cannot make your own lines, so the Power only works where nature provides them — jungle vines and the like.

name: Telekinesis
description: Move things within Distant Range with your mind, this rank standing in for Might, to attack, hold, lift or throw beings and objects. Also an active defence against ranged attacks: physical ones directly; energy ones only by putting an object in the way, rolling the lower of your rank and that object's Structure (or a vehicle's Body). Each extra object controlled at once lowers your effective rank by 1d, on top of the usual multiple action penalty.

power_cons.name: Impel
power_cons.description: You can shove objects in a straight line or hold them still, but fine manipulation is beyond you.

name: Telepathy
description: Read minds and send your thoughts to anyone within Distant Range. You sense sentient minds in range; a telepath who cloaks theirs must be beaten in an opposed Telepathy roll. Reading surface thoughts, or probing memories for something specific, is a Telepathy roll against the higher of the target's Willpower or Telepathy. Telepaths feel their thoughts being read; a probe takes a few minutes of total concentration and anybody can feel it. A probe reaches ordinary, repressed and altered memories.

power_pros.name: Alter Memories
power_pros.description: Roll 3 or more net successes on a mind probe and you can rewrite the subject's memories as you wish. The change lasts for the rest of the scene, or permanently if you spend 1 Resolve.

power_pros.name: Cloak Others
power_pros.description: You can hide the minds of everyone within Close Range of you from Telepathy, not only your own.

power_pros.name: Dream Travel
power_pros.description: You can enter and take part in the dreams of others. Inside a dream your physical Traits become the greater of your Willpower or Telepathy.

power_pros.name: Mind Link
power_pros.description: You can link minds up to your Power rank so all of them can talk to each other. They must stay within Extreme Range of you.

power_cons.name: Empathy
power_cons.description: You are limited to sensing and sending emotions and moods — never words or images.

name: Teleportation
description: Travel instantly, as far as the Teleportation table gives for your rank, through solid objects but not force fields. Somewhere you can see or know well is safe. For an unfamiliar place roll two dice: on a result of 6 or less the Power fails, you reappear where you started, and the shock knocks you out for the rest of the scene unless you spend 1 Resolve. Each use is a move, however far. Spend 1 Resolve to teleport twice in a page, using 1 action, within your maximum total distance.

power_pros.name: Portal
power_pros.description: You can open portals others can travel through.

power_cons.name: Medium
power_cons.description: You can only travel along or through some medium — power lines, shadows, reflective surfaces.

name: Time Stop
description: Stop time across the zone for as many pages as your rank, or until you release it. It costs 1 Resolve the first time in a scene, 2 the second, 3 the third and so on. Everyone and everything else in the area is frozen. You move freely and can reposition people and objects you have the Might to shift, but cannot otherwise affect or harm anything frozen. Forces still act on you, not on them. The GM may disallow it.

name: Time Travel
description: Spend an action to travel forward or back in time, as far as you like. Agree it with your GM first: they decide how time travel works in the setting, including whether changing the past changes the present, and may restrict it however they wish.

power_pros.name: Portal
power_pros.description: You can open portals others can travel through.

name: Total Recall
description: You remember whatever you paid attention to, with no roll. For a background detail you were not attending to, roll Intellect against a threshold the GM sets.

power_pros.name: Playback
power_pros.description: Common among cyborgs and robots: your memories can be copied, stored, moved elsewhere and shown to others.

name: Tracer
description: Tag an object you touch and you can follow it across the world until the story ends. No roll, unless it goes somewhere that blocks the Power, which may take an Intellect roll. Somebody who suspects a tag needs a Daunting (3) Perception roll to find it.

power_pros.name: Tracking
power_pros.description: An object the subject recently owned, or a place they visited in the last day or so, lets you track them as though you had tagged them.

name: Transformation — Animal Forms
description: Turn into any natural animal you know, living or extinct, taking its appearance, form, size and weight. You get its Agility, Might, Perception and Toughness and its Powers, each at the lower of its rank and yours. Magical creatures are the GM's call. Changing form is a free action on your own turn; at any other time it costs you your next turn.

power_pros.name: Enhanced
power_pros.description: When you take an animal's shape you may substitute your Power rank for that animal's highest-ranked Trait — one Trait per animal, your choice if several tie.

power_cons.name: Only X
power_cons.description: You can only become one category of animal, named at purchase. Worth more if it is a single animal or a very limited group.

name: Transformation — Doppelganger
description: Become an exact duplicate of anyone you have ever seen, provided they are roughly humanoid and close to your size. You pass biometric scanners and even DNA analysis, but gain none of their Abilities, Talents or Powers. Changing form is a free action on your own turn; at any other time it costs you your next turn.

name: Transformation — Object Forms
description: Turn into objects. As a simple shape you exert force or resistance at your rank. As a tool or weapon you add half your rank to the rolls of whoever uses you, their total capped at your rank. As a machine or vehicle you have its characteristics at the lower of its rank and yours. You can also be as large or small as Growth or Shrinking at this rank would make you, without changing your Traits. Changing form is a free action on your own turn; at any other time it costs you your next turn.

name: Transformation — Shapeshifting
description: Reshape your body at will. You have Hero Points equal to your rank to spend, temporarily, on raising Agility, Might and Toughness and on Powers for claws, wings, gills, tough hide and the like; nothing may pass the Trait Cap. For working out Resolve, this counts as your Shapeshifting rank plus your highest of Agility, Might and Toughness. Changing form is a free action on your own turn; at any other time it costs you your next turn.

name: Transmutation
description: Change the chemical make-up of inanimate matter you touch. Gas within Close Range is affected automatically; for a liquid or solid roll Transmutation against the greater of its Structure or weight rank. Raise Structure as high as your rank or lower it as far as you like, even turning solids to liquid or gas and back. Harmful substances you make act at your rank. Effects last until the scene ends or you dismiss them; 1 Resolve makes one permanent, and 1 Resolve is also the price of creating a material unique to the setting.

name: Vanish
description: Disappear in an instant and move as far as one page allows without anybody seeing where you went. It uses both an action, to vanish, and your movement, to get away.

name: Tunneling
description: A Travel Power: your rank is your top speed digging through the ground. Collapse the tunnel behind you or leave it open for others to follow. Nothing shows on the surface, which makes it a good way to surprise people.

name: Two-Dimensional
description: Become flat, like a shadow: weightless and silent, yet the three-dimensional world still affects you, and you it. As well as moving normally you can slide along any surface, ignoring gravity, and slip through any crack wide enough for your outline.

name: Two-Fisted
description: Spend 1 Resolve on a physical attack to defeat 2 Minions per net success instead of 1; you may decide after you roll. No gain on attacks that already do so — area attacks, Super Speed attacks, the Ricochet Pro. Wielding two mundane weapons also adds +1d to their Weapon Bonus, which does not apply to Powers with the Item or Weapons Con. It never grants extra attacks.

power_cons.name: Fighting/Marksmanship
power_cons.description: Bought as Fighting, the Power works only in close combat and its Weapon Bonus only on melee weapons; as Marksmanship, only in ranged combat and only on ranged weapons.

name: Variant
description: A different version of a Power you already have. You pay a flat 3 Hero Points, but the Variant must be worth exactly what the original cost: a Variant that does more has to carry Cons that make up the difference. Not available for any Power that affects other Traits — Boost, Drain, Nullify, Power Absorption and Power Mimicry among them — nor for Alternate Form, Elemental Control or Omni-Power.
notes: Costs a flat 3 Hero Points but must be worth as many Hero Points as the Power it varies — the difference has to be made up with Cons. Cannot vary Alternate Form and several other Powers.

name: Ventriloquism
description: Mimic almost any sound, imitate other people convincingly, and throw your voice so it seems to come from somewhere else. Roll Charm, usually against the target's Perception.

name: Wall-Crawling
description: Stick to walls and ceilings and move along them at your normal speed. If this rank is below your Might, it sets how much weight you can carry while doing so. An unusually slick surface may call for a Wall-Crawling roll.

name: Weakness Detection
description: Study a person or object in person to find its weak points. Spend 1 Resolve and your physical and energy attacks have the Penetrating Pro against it for the rest of the scene. At no cost, it also gives you narrative information about an object's structural flaws and stress points.
